scenes.say: Why does the eye doctor put drops in your eyes before the check-up? Here's what to expect.

scenes.en: Drops widen the pupil so the retina and optic nerve can be seen clearly.
scenes.say: The drops widen your pupil, the black circle in the middle. It's like opening a door wider, so the doctor can see the retina and the optic nerve at the back of your eye.

scenes.en: A dilated exam can spot early diabetic eye changes, glaucoma and retinal tears.
scenes.say: Did you know? A dilated eye exam can catch early signs of diabetic eye disease, glaucoma and retinal tears, often before you notice any problem.

scenes.en: Blurry up close and light-sensitive for a few hours.
scenes.ta: சில மணி நேரம் மங்கலாகவும், வெளிச்சம் கூசவும் செய்யும்
scenes.say: After the drops, near vision is blurry, and bright light feels harsh for a few hours. That is normal.

scenes.ta: வண்டி ஓட்ட வேண்டாம். ஒருவரை கூட்டி வாருங்கள்
scenes.say: So don't drive or ride a bike home. Bring someone with you, and carry sunglasses.

scenes.en: Keep the next few hours light. Pain or redness that lasts? Call the eye specialist.
scenes.ta: முன்பே திட்டமிடுங்கள். வலி நீடித்தால் மருத்துவரை அழையுங்கள்
scenes.say: Keep the next few hours light, without much reading or screen work. If eye pain, redness or blurred vision lasts beyond the day, call the eye specialist.
If you're over forty, or have diabetes, regular eye checks matter. Book an eye test today.
